concept_text: A retail company is integrating Amazon Bedrock into an existing e-commerce platform to power a generative AI (GenAI) application. To automate product listing creation, the team designed a multi-agent workflow using AWS Step Functions. Three agents run in sequence: a content creator, a technical validator, and a brand alignment reviewer, each building on the reasoning traces and outputs of the previous agent. All processing artifacts and final outputs are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. During a testing phase, the team begins seeing consistent workflow failures. Investigation reveals that intermediate payloads passed between states regularly exceed the 256 KB Step Functions quota, halting execution before completion. To address this, a GenAI Engineer is tasked with reworking the architecture so that large payloads no longer trigger execution failures. The solution must also retain end-to-end workflow observability and maintain the multi-agent reasoning and acting (ReAct) pattern. Which of the following architectural modifications fulfills these specifications while minimizing operational overhead? || RESPUESTA: Update the optimized Bedrock API calls to ingest large payloads directly from a S3 URI. Extract the newly generated S3 object locations using ResultSelector and append these lightweight pointers to the state payload using ResultPath, enabling the seamless chaining of agents without breaching payload quotas.

concept_text: A company operates a global e-learning marketplace that helps learners discover courses and instructors. concept_text: A research group operates TD Owl, a secure analytics platform that processes highly confidential regulatory documents, internal valuation reports, and sensitive liquidity forecasts.
